_doc: THE MANAGER LEASE. Exactly one management session at a time, never two.
Written by scripts/ops/manager_lease.py -- do not hand-edit; a hand-edit that
breaks the JSON reads as `unreadable`, which REFUSES every claim until it is
READ THIS FILE BEFORE MANAGING ANYTHING:  python3 scripts/ops/manager_lease.py status
Takeover is TIME-BASED. A session that dies cannot hand over, so nothing here
depends on the outgoing manager cooperating. An outgoing manager still alive
learns at its next heartbeat that it no longer holds the lease, and stands down.
A CLAIM YOU DID NOT PUSH PROTECTS NOTHING -- another session reads `origin`.
Sub-sessions do NOT depend on this. They keep running with no lease held; what
pauses is SUPERVISION. docs/claude/work/SESSIONS.json is what a cold manager
reads to pick them up. Design: docs/claude/work/objects/WO-20260901-PHASE-E.yaml
note: Heartbeat 00:58:30Z, tool-stamped. ⚠️ THE MERGE QUEUE WAS BLOCKED REPO-WIDE, AND NOT BY ANY PR. `digest-liveness-guard` failed on #11473 with `state=stale last_digest_age=6.01h` against a 6h window. It is a TIME-based guard reading a repo-wide condition, so it reds EVERY PR until a digest lands — #11473's own summary line reads PASS 71 · FAIL 1, and that 1 is not its diff. Nothing in that PR could fix it, and nothing in any PR could. || THIS IS THE DOCUMENTED OI-20260902-HOURLY-DIGEST-CARRIER-PREPARED-AND-HELD-FOR-A-TIER-2-OK CONDITION SHOWING ITS COST: work-digest.yml declares `20 * * * *` and was measured firing 5 times a day, never on its declared minute. The durable fix — moving it onto the VM's own clock via deploy/ict-work-digest.timer — is PR #10858, Tier-2, and HELD on an operator OK. That hold is legitimate and I have not touched it. What was NOT visible before tonight is that the missing cadence does not merely cost the operator a digest: it periodically DEADLOCKS the whole merge queue. || WHAT I DID: dispatched work-digest.yml on main (workflow_dispatch, the workflow's own header says that trigger exists so the observation can be forced rather than waited for). ⚠️ A DISPATCH RUN IS NOT A CRON RUN and must not be recorded as one — the header names that exact substitution as what left two other workflows dead. This unblocks the queue by making the guard's real condition TRUE (a digest actually reaching the operator); it is a workaround, it proves nothing about the cadence, and OI-20260902 stays open and unchanged. || #11473 is NOT stalled and its session is NOT at fault: it merged main in at 00:42:33Z, CI re-fired, and it is IDLE/review_ready having correctly diagnosed the blocker itself ('#11473 blocked by repo deadlock'). No poke sent — there is nothing for it to fix. || VERIFIED ON MAIN 01:25Z, after #11477 merged at 01:04:29Z: `digest-liveness: OK state=fresh last_digest_age=0.44h` read against origin/main. The diagnosis held and the deadlock is cleared. ⚠️ THE CLEARANCE EXPIRES — the guard goes stale again ~6h after that receipt, around 07:04Z, and reds every PR again. Four stuck receipt PRs remain (#11442 #11445 #11452 #11465). MI-208 is the durable fix and is ROUTED to a session, not taken. || ⚠️ AND A NEAR-MISS ON THIS BRANCH, RECORDED BECAUSE IT WAS ONE COMMAND FROM DESTROYING THIS PR: I ran `git reset --hard origin/main` while standing ON this branch rather than on main, which silently rewound it and discarded b387dd1e + 24aa0e19 locally. The next commit was built on main's tree, so a force-push would have wiped the heartbeat, the deadlock finding and MI-208 while reporting success. Caught by reading `git log --oneline -1` and noticing it named MAIN's head on a branch that should have been two commits ahead. Recovered with `git reset --hard origin/<branch>` and re-verified: 208 checklist items, MI-208 present, arming pair present. The lesson is narrow and worth keeping: `reset --hard origin/main` is only ever safe when the CURRENT branch is main, and `git branch --show-current` costs nothing.
